mathematics.independent_solution: From the selected theorem, V=pi*d^3/6. Thus lambda=V'/V=(d'/d)^3 and, since d,d'>0, d'/d=cuberoot(lambda). The increment ratio is d'/d-1. Under final volume 2V it is cuberoot(2)-1; under increase 2V the final volume is 3V and it is cuberoot(3)-1. The explicitly conditional question has the unique complete true set {B}. Neither result resolves the original source phrase.

option_checks.evidence: It asserts d'/d=lambda, hence a volume ratio lambda^3 rather than lambda for every lambda>1. The listed increments 1 and 2 are precisely what the erroneous linear rule gives at final ratios 2 and 3.
d'/d=cuberoot(lambda) satisfies (d'/d)^3=lambda. Subtracting 1 gives cuberoot(2)-1 for final volume 2V and cuberoot(3)-1 for an increase of 2V; all three statements are true.

It takes a square root, as if volume scaled like diameter squared. Its proposed diameter multiplier gives volume ratio lambda^(3/2), not lambda for lambda>1; sqrt(2)-1 and sqrt(3)-1 follow that same wrong procedure.

The general cube-root diameter ratio is true, but the two stated increments omit subtraction of 1. cuberoot(2) and cuberoot(3) are final diameter multipliers, not the specified (d'-d)/d, so the complete group is false.
